clusters.title: The generic product carries one operator's migration and acceptance: memory import and verify, the import/ allowlist, the memory-entry and repo evidence kinds, tools/ci acceptance --file, and the C1 hugo check.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter (00 0.2) installs a product whose reference documents commands and an evidence kind that apply to nobody but the author, and whose block B acceptance includes C1, a check of a tool they do not use.
clusters.change: Delete julieta memory import and verify, the import/ allowlist entry, the memory-entry digest kind, the repo evidence kind, the --file flag and C1 (11 11.2's sandbox-side table then lists C2 to C5 and says 'Four checks'); move the one-time import to a script in the operator's config repo (02 2.2 already allows an operator acceptance.json there) and the predecessor archiving to an operator step outside the product. If kept, 00 0.5 states why a generic product needs each, and the reference marks them operator-only.
clusters.cost: Deletions in 00, 03, 04, 08, 10 and 11; the plan loses T058 and parts of T082 and T090; one script outside the product repo.
clusters.resolution_text: Changes the scope (00 0.5 records the maintainer's decision that pre-v1 memory entries are imported once at adoption), so the operator decides. Recommendation: delete from the product and move to the operator's config repo; page 11's share is removing C1, with its id left unused per 11 11.1's rule.
clusters.operator_reason: Reverses a scope decision recorded in 00 0.5 and removes acceptance items the operator chose.

clusters.title: Block A 'needs no product code', yet A3's Expect requires romeu/julieta checks and ledger ingest, and A5 records hashes of render goldens before render exists.
clusters.scenario: At block O3 (end of phase 1) memstore, julieta memory check and ingest do not exist; A3 is inconclusive or its predicate is narrowed at the host, I24/I32/I33 stay unsettled with nothing recording it, or the sitting waits for phase 5. The A5 goldens are hand-written and the renderer is later bent to match them.
clusters.change: Split A3. A3 keeps the mount facts: Expect becomes 'each plant is seen on the host as planted; no write reaches the host through a readOnly mount, also as root after remount; no write reaches the primary host clone; each mount path equals the host path'; Settles: the read-only host clone (02 2.3), I30, and the mount half of I24 and I32. Add a block B sandbox-side check C6 (11 11.2): 'from inside, the A3 plants in a memory dir and the spool; julieta memory check and the romeu checks report every plant; ingest skips each spool plant with its reason and does not block'; it settles I24, I32, I33 and julieta delivery (06 6.3); the table intro says 'Six checks'. To 11 11.1's opening add: 'The A5 goldens are written by hand with the probe definitions; render (12 12.2) must reproduce them byte for byte, and tools/ci probes already flags a moved hash.'
clusters.cost: One row split, one new C row, one sentence; the plan's question 6 already asks it.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed: A3 keeps only the mount facts, the product half becomes C6 in block B, and 11 11.1's opening states that the A5 goldens are hand-written first and render must reproduce them.

clusters.title: An overturned result fails tools/ci probes, a step of all, so the pull request that commits block A results cannot merge until the fix, its ADR and resolvedBy ride with it, unlike 10 10.5's end-only check of S6 rows.
clusters.scenario: O3 returns with A10 overturning the secrets apply tag; the results PR is red until a code change to internal/spec/project.go (a gates surface, with its own approvals) and an ADR join it; the other eleven results and the 54 tasks waiting on block A wait on it.
clusters.change: In 11 11.4 change the overturned row's Check to 'tools/ci acceptance fails while any result is overturned' and add after the table: 'tools/ci probes, a step of all, checks the schema, the computed decision and, once resolvedBy is set, the resolved row; an overturned result does not fail it, so results land as soon as they are measured and the fix lands in its own pull request, like an S6 row before its code (10 10.5).'
clusters.cost: One cell and one sentence; the plan's question 9 already asks it before T020.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply L12-15's form (move the failure to tools/ci acceptance), which reuses the existing end-only check instead of L9-12's coupling of the fix to the results PR; the resolved-row checks stay in tools/ci probes.

clusters.title: Probe results never go stale: they record the sbx version but nothing compares it with the floor, the agent version behind C3 and C5 is not recorded, and no rule says which pin bump re-runs which probe.
clusters.scenario: The sbx floor is bumped (10 10.3 commits a new recording set) or the Claude Code pin moves; tools/ci probes passes on results that never saw the new version; Q22, settled by C5 and gone from the Open questions table, and the J5 guide still describe the old hook order.
clusters.change: In 11 11.3 add to host an 'upstream' map: the version of each upstream the probe reads beyond sbx (the frontend pin for A11 to A13, the agent version for C3 and C5), recorded by the harness. In 11 11.4 add: 'A result is a fact about the versions its host records. tools/ci acceptance fails when a block A result's sbxVersion differs from the floor of 10 10.3, or a recorded upstream differs from its current pin; a floor or pin bump therefore re-runs the probes that read it before the next release, and the new result re-settles their open questions.' In 11 11.3's affects rule add: 'including each docs/guide page that narrates the result; tools/ci probes fails when a guide page names a probe id its affects does not list.'
clusters.cost: One result field, two clauses in existing checks, three sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply without a new 'stale' state or per-version file names: the version comparison joins tools/ci acceptance and git history keeps the superseded results; the guide clause covers L8-19's affects half.

clusters.title: Block A measures none of the sandbox events salvage and a working month rely on: exec on a stopped sandbox, a Docker or daemon restart with a sandbox running, the signing socket afterwards, sbx env rm and the workload's volumes, an sbx upgrade under existing sandboxes.
clusters.scenario: On real sbx, exec on a stopped sandbox fails instead of starting it, or sbx env rm deletes the per-name volumes, or the signing socket does not return after a restart; the J6 and J10 salvage designs and 01 1.6 meet it first in block B or in a user's report.
clusters.change: Add A15 to 11 11.1: Probe 'on a detached env sandbox: sbx stop, then sbx env exec; restart Docker with the sandbox running and run sbx ls --json during and after; ssh-add -L inside after the restart; sbx env rm and list the workload's volumes'; Expect 'exec on a stopped sandbox recorded (starts it or fails); state and fields reported across the restart recorded; the signing socket returns; volumes after rm recorded'; Settles '01 1.6, 08 8.5'. Add after the table: 'An sbx upgrade under existing sandboxes cannot be staged on demand; it is measured when the floor moves (11 11.4's version rule re-runs block A).'
clusters.cost: One probe, about 15 minutes per host.
clusters.resolution_text: One probe A15 for the stop, restart and rm facts; the upgrade case is stated as a limit, measured at the next floor bump (R8-11-4), and the stopped-disk-from-host read is dropped.

clusters.title: The v1.0.0 binaries are a second build declared the same as the candidate's only by argument from pins, with no build contract and no check, and the post-tag B1 run starts no sandbox.
clusters.scenario: A toolchain or flag difference between the two Actions runs changes an embedded kit's digest; S3, S5 and S7 were measured on the candidate; v1.0.0 users meet gate 2 on every project, and nobody can reproduce the published binary from the tag.
clusters.change: Add to 10 10.2: 'tools/release build uses -trimpath, CGO_ENABLED=0, a fixed build id and the commit time as build date, and writes archives with fixed mtimes, owners and order, in the scrubbed environment of the tools/ci steps.' In 11 11.2 replace 'the pins ... are what makes the second build the same as the first' with 'the pins and the build contract of 10 10.2 aim to make the second build the same as the first; nothing compares the bytes', and change 'the maintainer runs B1 once more' to 'runs B1 and B2 once more, on v1.0.0 and on one host'.
clusters.cost: One sentence in 10 10.2, two edits in 11 11.2, about 15 more minutes at the post-tag sitting.
clusters.resolution_text: Fix the build contract and extend the post-tag run to B2 on one host; a byte-for-byte rebuild check is not added and the spec says so.

clusters.title: The docs-only difference between the candidate's commit and the v1.0.0 tag is checked only by tools/ci acceptance after the tag, which cannot be redone, and before it only by the maintainer remembering.

clusters.change: In 11 11.2 after 'tools/ci acceptance checks that for each block B result' add: 'release.yml runs the same comparison first on a tag without a suffix, against the candidate the committed block B results name, and fails the release before it builds.' Name the step in 10 10.2's release.yml description.
clusters.cost: One workflow step reusing the acceptance comparison; two sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the pre-tag check for the candidate comparison. The finding's second half (the security log at each sitting, 05 5.4) is not on this page and touches an accepted risk; it belongs to the 05 consolidation.
